title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-scratchpad
body:
Notes / scratchpad for pricing + packaging. Very rough - mostly to align on unit economics and a few tier sketches.

Context: we need simple, predictable hosted pricing for self-serve that (a) covers COGS + infra + support + ~30-40% margin and (b) gives clear signal when customers should move to Dedicated/Private. Also need anchor prices for embeddings vs. generation and for model variants (small/med/large).

Assumptions / inputs (rough):
- GPU types we use for hosted: A100-equivalent (spot/pooled) avg cost (incl infra + amortized infra overhead) = $3.00 / GPU-hour effective for inference (after pooling/batching savings) - placeholder
- Average throughput per GPU: 20k tokens/sec sustained (batching + KV cache helps) -> 72M tokens/hour per GPU (20k * 3600)
- Effective tokens served per GPU-hour (accounting utilization/inefficiencies): assume 50% -> 36M tokens/hour
- So raw COGS per token = $3.00 / 36M = $8.3e-8 $/token ≈ $0.000000083/token
- For ease, scale to per-1M tokens: $0.083 per 1M tokens (raw GPU only)
- Add infra overhead (control plane, storage, networking, ops, monitoring) ~ +50% -> $0.125 per 1M tokens
- Add S&M + support allocation + amortized R&D overhead and margin target -> multiply by 3x total -> target list price ≈ $0.375 per 1M tokens (~$0.38)

Quick sanity check: existing market comps: many vendors ~ $0.2-$2.0 per 1M tokens depending on model. Our $0.38 sits in lower-mid range for good perf models - seems plausible for a baseline small/medium model.

Per-request economics (example):
- Typical chat request: prompt 100 tokens + response 300 tokens = 400 tokens total
- Cost per request (COGS) at $0.125 / 1M tokens = 400 * 0.125 / 1e6 = $0.00005 (~0.005 cents)
- List price with markup (x3) -> $0.00015 per request (0.015 cents)

Embeddings:
- Embedding model cheaper per compute (smaller model or optimized kernel). Assume effective per-1k-embedding cost = $0.05 (COGS) -> list price with markup ~ $0.15 per 1k embeddings.

Dedicated / Reserved capacity thinking (back of envelope):
- Dedicated customers pay for reserved GPU capacity. Offer pricing as $/GPU-hour committed or flat monthly per-GPU.
- If we price Dedicated at e.g. $2.40 / GPU-hour effective (20% discount vs hosted list), that implies commitment needed to make COGS coverage stable. But actually Dedicated should be priced higher to reflect SLA, isolation and lower multi-tenant gains -> maybe $2.8-$3.5 / GPU-hour depending on SLA and support.
- Need simple translation: for customers serving N tokens/month, estimate equivalent GPU-hours = tokens / tokens_per_hour_per_gpu_eff. Example: 1B tokens/mo -> 1,000 * ($ per 1M tokens) = if priced hosted at $0.38/1M -> $380/mo. Equivalent GPU hours = 1B / 36M ≈ 27.8 GPU-hours -> that implies hosted is much cheaper than Dedicated per-GPU-month so this calculation is wrong dimensionally - wait: re-evaluate.
  - 1B tokens/mo / 36M tokens/hour = 27.8 GPU-hours total (this is suspiciously low). Error: 36M tokens/hour per GPU -> to serve 1B tokens you'd need ~27.8 hours of GPU time only - that seems low. But indeed 1B tokens ~ ~277 GPU-hours? Let's compute carefully: 36M tokens/hour -> to serve 1B tokens: 1,000M / 36M ≈ 27.78 hours. That suggests each GPU hour handles 36M tokens. So 1B tokens require 28 GPU-hours - plausible if GPU throughput assumptions high. But reality: throughput depends on model size, latency constraints, and many requests small. So for latency-sensitive low-latency workloads effective utilization is much lower. For conservative sizing use 5M tokens/hour per GPU (50% less) or even 1-2M for very chatty workloads.
  - If we assume 5M tokens/hour per GPU -> 1B / 5M = 200 GPU-hours -> monthly cost at $3/GPU-hour = $600. That aligns more with expectation.

So include conservative throughput buckets:
- aggressive (batched large requests): 36M tokens/hr
- typical mixed usage: 5M tokens/hr
- worst-case interactive low-batching: 1M tokens/hr

Use these to show when Dedicated makes sense:
- Example: customer uses 100B tokens/mo. At hosted price $0.38/1M -> $38k/mo. Equivalent conservative GPU-hours (5M/hr): 100,000M / 5M = 20,000 GPU-hours -> cost at $3/GPU-hour = $60k COGS -> difference shows hosted list price needs to be set carefully. This indicates our earlier per-1M numbers may understate COGS if throughput assumption too optimistic.

Tier sketch (self-serve hosted):
- Free: 100k tokens/month + 1k embeddings / month, limited rate, no SLA.
- Developer (pay-as-you-go): $10/month credit + usage at $0.50 per 1M tokens (cheap anchor) OR $0.20 per 1M for small model and $0.50 per 1M for large model. Maybe simpler: single usage price $0.38/1M (baseline) but also offer monthly bundles.
- Starter / Team: $49/mo includes 20M tokens + overage $0.35/1M; includes basic dashboards, 30d logs retention.
- Business: $499/mo includes 500M tokens + overage $0.30/1M; includes priority support, 90d retention, can request Dedicated evaluation credits.
- Enterprise: custom price, Dedicated options, volume discounts, SLA, VPC/private.

Pricing levers to test:
- Model-based pricing (small/med/large) vs. unified pricing (easier to understand).
- Bundles vs. pure usage. Bundles help with predictable revenue and reduce churn but add complexity for servo UX.
- Per-conversation or per-session pricing (for apps where tokens not a good signal) - tough b/c varying lengths.

Embeddings-specific tiering:
- Pay-as-you-go: $0.15 / 1k embeddings (list)
- Bulk: $100/mo includes up to 1M embeddings, overage $0.10 / 1k
- Dedicated embedding service: flat monthly + per-index storage fee.

Things to validate / TODOs:
- Re-run COGS with accurate infra numbers (A100 vs. 4090, on-demand vs. reserved, region differences) - current $3/GPU-hour is a placeholder.
- Get realistic tokens/hour per GPU for our actual inference runtime across model sizes and sequences (SRE/Serving to provide perf profs per model).
- Model size breakpoints and cost multipliers for small/med/large (e.g., 7b ~ x1, 13b ~ x1.5, 70b ~ x3).
- Behavioral data: distribution of request sizes (prompt/response), session lengths, embedding vs. generation mix.
- Customer willingness to pay tests for bundles vs pure usage.
- Competitive price survey (top 5 rivals) with exact model mapping.

Open questions / notes to myself:
- How do we communicate quantization / perf variants? Possibly price-by-performance tiers (fast/cheap vs high-quality) and expose conversion guidance.
- For Dedicated: pricing should reflect cheaper per-GPU cost for committed monthly buys but added ops/support overhead + SLA. Maybe list dedicated baseline and offer discount for multi-month commits.
- Consider a simple metering UX: daily burn estimate, tokens forecast, burst protection to avoid surprise bills.

Draft messaging hooks:
- "Pay only for inference you use - predictable per-1M pricing with clear upgrade path to Dedicated for high-volume workloads."
- "Bundles for teams: predictable spend, lower unit costs, easy upgrade to Dedicated."

Rough next steps:
1) Get precise perf data from serving-runtime team for 3 representative models (7b, 13b, 70b): tokens/hr, avg latency under typical batch sizes. (owner: @Emily)
2) Cost model: infra procurement + cloud costs + SRE ops overhead -> compute COGS per token for each model. (owner: finance/pricing)
3) Build simple pricing simulator that maps tokens/month -> hosted bill vs Dedicated commitment (owner: me)
4) Run internal pricing sensitivity / willingness to pay with sample customers / field reps.

Notes end.

Scratchy notes / random thoughts:
- might want to have a small flat monthly developer seat price ($9-$15) to reduce friction vs pure usage for low-volume devs.
- Consider an "auto-upgrade" prompt when usage crosses X tokens/day suggesting Dedicated evaluation.
- For private deployments, price as platform fee + per-GPU or per-host license.

TODO: tidy into a PRD + examples and send to Pricing sync.
